row.evidence: Raygun's SSO docs say SAML SSO is free on Business and Enterprise (a $50/month add-on otherwise) and that provisioning works by creating the account on first SSO sign-in, with de-provisioning done by contacting Raygun or removing the team member; no SCIM is offered.
row.notes: Status unchanged (none). Usage-priced per module, not per user: Crash Reporting Basic $40, Team $80, Business $400 per month on annual billing (save 33% vs monthly $60/$120/$600), Enterprise custom; unlimited members on all plans. SAML SSO is included on Business and Enterprise and is a $50/month add-on on other plans. Provisioning is JIT on SAML sign-in only; removal is manual. Okta's OIN Raygun app is SWA only. The Raygun API v3 (personal access tokens, all plans) can list teams and send/revoke invitations but cannot list or remove members.

scim.notes: No SCIM in pricing, the documentation sitemap or the SSO page; SSO page says provisioning is JIT on first SSO sign-in and deprovisioning is manual. Recorded as none by absence.

capabilities.notes: Teams can be listed but not modified; no member list or removal endpoint in the API endpoint table.

rate_limits.text: 10 calls per second, 600 per minute, 10,000 per day

user_api.notes: The Raygun API (all plans) is a data API; for people it only lists teams and sends/revokes invitations. No endpoints to list, update or remove members, so it is not counted as a user-management API.

okta.notes: OIN Raygun app marks SWA only; Raygun's docs say to build a custom Okta SAML app.

entra.notes: Custom SAML app configuration; JIT only.

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: Crash Reporting module; unlimited members. SAML SSO available as a $50/month add-on below Business. Raygun API included but has no member-management endpoints beyond invitations.
